overview_description.description:
ROSS Intelligence builds artificially intelligent tools to enhance lawyer’s abilities – allowing them to do more than ever before humanly possible. Their vision is to create the world’s smartest lawyer. Their first product, ROSS, is an artificially intelligent lawyer.

ROSS Intelligence's customers include many of the top law firms and corporate legal departments, both in the United States and abroad. ROSS Intelligence transforms lawyers' workflow with artificial intelligence.

ROSS Intelligence operates out of Toronto, San Francisco, and New York.

press_references.value: AI Company Battles Thomson Reuters Over Copyright

legal_proceedings.description: Thomson Reuters is pursuing a copyright infringement lawsuit against Ross Intelligence over the use of Westlaw headnotes to train Ross's AI legal research product; Ross is appealing a district court ruling that found it infringed copyright and rejected its fair use defense.

press_references.value: AI’s Copyright Conundrum: Legal Battles Reshaping Tech’s Future

legal_proceedings.description: In Thomson Reuters v. Ross Intelligence, a U.S. judge rejected Ross’s fair‑use defense for training on copyrighted data, a setback for the AI legal research startup.

press_references.value: Jack Dorsey Says Intellectual Property Law Shouldn't Exist, and Elon Musk Agrees: 'Delete All IP Law' Dorsey stated that the legal system was currently inhibiting creativity.

legal_proceedings.description: Jack Dorsey and Elon Musk advocate for the abolition of intellectual property law, arguing it inhibits creativity. This stance comes amid ongoing legal battles where copyright holders have sued AI companies like OpenAI, Google, and Meta for using copyrighted work without permission. A recent U.S. court ruling against Ross Intelligence rejected the fair use defense for using copyrighted material to train AI.

press_references.value: Generative AI Training Case Flags Competition as Major Factor

legal_proceedings.description: The Thomson Reuters v. Ross Intelligence case explores the application of the 'fair use' defense in copyright law for AI training, focusing on whether AI systems compete with copyrighted works.
